reasoning: Air bucket (overcards JTs) on dry rainbow 852 board, 3-way IP after both checks. Air bucket (KJ overcards) OOP first to act on Ace-high A93r flop that favours the BTN raiser. With no pair, no draw, and OOP into 2 opponents on a board that smashes BTN's range, hero has insufficient fold equity and dominated overcards. Standard check.

Drawing bucket (non-nut FD + gutshot). Per KB §1.7, semi-bluff RAISE 3-way requires nut draw + blocker; Td9d is non-nut FD with no Ace blocker, so raise carve-out fails. Getting 26.8% pot odds with ~36% draw equity plus the gutshot side equity, calling realises equity and avoids the unprofitable semi-bluff raise.

Air bucket (missed OESD, 9-high no SDV) on river facing checked action. Per DO NOT Rule 2, 3-way fold equity is ~36% — pure river bluffs lose money, and 9-high cannot value-bet. Check and accept the loss.

Drawing bucket (nut FD with Ad blocker + 2 overcards K/A). This is the canonical KB §1.7 / Worked Example 9 pattern: nut flush draw + blocker to villain's nut combos + side equity facing single c-bet 3-way. Solver-verified RAISE; the Ad blocker generates the fold equity needed above the 3-way break-even, and the combo gives ~40%+ when called. CALL is the alternative but wastes the blocker's fold equity.

Drawing bucket (non-nut FD Qd3d, no Ace blocker, no straight draw). Per KB §1.7, the raise carve-out requires nut FD + blocker; Qd3d fails both. Getting 26.8% pot odds with ~36% flush-completion equity, calling realises equity at the right price; raising would lose to villain's continuing range that includes the nut flush draws hero doesn't block.

Monster bucket (flopped nut straight Tc9c on QhJs8d). 3-way IP checked through to hero on a wet connected board where draws and two pair are abundant in villain ranges. Per KB §1.4 and Section 2 Factor 4, monsters on dynamic boards must build the pot and charge equity; 66% pot extracts from sets, two pair, and combo draws while protecting against the many straight/flush turns.

Medium-made bucket (TPGK QJ on Q83r dry rainbow). 3-way IP after both opponents checked = weakness signal. Per Worked Example 2 (thin value IP with air-heavy villain range), a small 25% bet extracts from worse Qx, pocket pairs, and air on a low-danger dry board. DO NOT Rule 11 doesn't apply (board not paired or 2-tone-flush).

Medium-made bucket (TPGK QJ on Q83r) but OOP first to act 3-way. Per Equity Realization (Section 1.5), OOP under-realizes (60-80%) and per DO NOT Rule 5 top pair is medium-strength 3-way. Checking pot-controls and lets hero check-call bets; betting OOP into 2 live opponents risks isolating into better Qx or being raised.

Strong-made bucket (overpair JJ on 962r dry rainbow). 3-way IP after both checks shows weakness, board has no overpairs in opponents' continuing ranges (QQ+ would 3-bet preflop). A small 25% protective bet extracts thin value from underpairs and worse pairs (9x, 6x), denies equity to the many overcard hands, and DO NOT Rule 11 doesn't fire (rainbow unpaired board).

Strong-made bucket (overpair JJ on 962r) OOP first to act 3-way. Board is dry rainbow so DO NOT Rule 11 doesn't fire; with 2 live opponents and many overcards in ranges (K, A, Q, T), a small 25% bet denies equity and protects equity-realisation OOP. CHECK is the alternative for pot control but hero's strong-made hand benefits from charging the air-and-overcard heavy ranges to act.

Medium-made bucket (TPGK KT on KdJc6s) facing bet+call. Per the v2 reversal anchor in v3.4 Calibration Notes, MW-30 is solver-verified CALL: 40% raw equity well above 18.4% pot odds, and the BTN cold-caller's continuing range still contains <40% TP+ with significant medium-made and weaker holdings KT beats. Equity surplus overrides the bet-and-call narrowing signal.

Monster bucket (flopped middle set 88 on 873r) facing bet+call. Per the v2 reversal anchor in v3.4 Calibration Notes, MW-33 is RAISE: sets must raise vs bet+call for value extraction on a wet connected board where straight draws and two pair are plentiful. Just calling lets turns destroy equity (one-card straights/two-pair improvements); raising 66% charges draws and builds the pot.

Strong-made bucket (overpair AA on J94r) — hero is the preflop aggressor c-betting into 3-way after BB check. Per KB §1.3, default 3-way c-bet sizing is 25-33% when hero's range advantage is meaningful; AA on a board with no overpairs in opponents' ranges (KK+ 3-bet preflop) extracts thin value from Jx and pocket pairs while denying equity to overcards. Small 25% bet is the canonical PFA play.

Medium-made bucket (TPGK QJ on Q72r dry) facing single CO c-bet at compressed SPR ~3, hero IP. Equity well above 25% pot odds and TPGK has strong showdown value on a dry rainbow board. Calling keeps villain's bluffs in and lets hero realise SDV; raising at compressed SPR over-commits with a hand that doesn't want to play a huge pot.

Medium-made bucket (TPGK QJ on Q72r dry) at standard SPR ~8 facing CO c-bet. Same hand-type analysis as MW-35: ~26% pot odds with TPGK on a dry static board easily clears hero's required equity. Hero realises showdown value across multiple streets; folding is way too tight given board favours hero's range and villain's c-bet range includes plenty of air.

Medium-made bucket (TPGK QJ on Q72r) at deep SPR ~15 facing CO c-bet. Deep stacks amplify reverse-implied-odds for TPGK and Equity Realization Section 1.5 says deep multiway disfavours under-realising hands. Still, ~25% pot odds and TPGK on dry rainbow clears the required equity threshold; calling once and re-evaluating turn is the standard play. FOLD considered but rejected — CO's c-bet range still contains too much air and worse Qx.

Drawing bucket (nut FD AhJh + Ah blocker + overcard J) IP at compressed SPR ~3 facing BB donk. KB §1.7 carve-out conditions met (nut FD + Ah blocker + side equity). At low SPR, raising commits stacks but the nut FD + blocker generates real fold equity AND ~40%+ when called; CALL is the alternative but wastes fold equity at SPR where villain folds underpairs/weak Kx to pressure. Difficulty 3 — close between RAISE and CALL.

Drawing bucket (nut FD AhJh + Ah blocker + overcard J) IP at deep SPR ~15 facing CO c-bet. Per v3.2 KB §1.7 OVERRIDE (Fix 2), the nut FD + blocker → RAISE carve-out is suspended when villain_air_pct < 0.20; in this 3-way bet-alone-multiway with deep SPR, fold equity is structurally insufficient (CO bet alone, no second narrowing). CALL realises equity vs villain's calling range and preserves implied odds when the flush hits.

Medium-made bucket (Q with T kicker on KQ7-J = middle pair + gutshot to broadway) facing CO turn double-barrel 3-way. Per Section 4 Factor 5, multi-street aggression (villain_aggression_count = 2) narrows CO's range to TP+ (Kx with kickers, KQ, sets, AK). Hero's ~22-25% combined equity vs the narrowed range is below 23% pot odds and middle pair Q is dominated by villain's TP+ density. CALL considered but rejected — equity is too thin against the narrowed double-barrel range.

Medium-made bucket (TP T8 + OESD turn on T947 = 8 outs to straight + made pair). BB's double lead is unusual but hero has substantial combo equity (~40%+ to improve plus showdown). 28% pot odds easily clear hero's draw + made hand equity; calling keeps the straight outs alive and lets hero realise SDV. RAISE considered but rejected — BB's polarised donk range and CO behind both argue against ballooning the pot OOP-relative.

Air bucket (gutshot K + overcard A on QJ4r). OOP first to act 3-way at compressed SPR ~2. Per DO NOT Rule 2, semi-bluffing 3-way without nut draw + blocker is unprofitable; gutshot + 1 overcard doesn't qualify and OOP into 2 live opponents at low SPR amplifies the cost. Check and realise equity; backdoor improvement and SDV from A-high may be enough on later streets.

Strong-made bucket (TPTK AdKd on A95-T turn). Hero bet flop and got two callers, then turn checked through to hero IP. Both callers have strong continuing ranges but TPTK still beats most of them (worse Ax, mid pairs, draws). Per Section 4 Factor 5, after flop bet-call-call hero must continue value/protection on turn; 75% pot extracts from worse Ax and charges flush + straight draws on the connecting T turn.

Medium-made bucket (TP J with T kicker on J84-5) facing BTN turn bet AFTER BTN raised flop. Per the v2 reversal anchor in v3.4 Calibration Notes, MW-50 is FOLD: BTN's flop raise narrowed range to TP+ (better Jx, sets, two pair), and turn continuation maintains that strength. Hero's TP weak kicker is dominated and there's no nut blocker or strong draw to support a continue. Action history overrides raw equity.

Medium-made bucket (TPGK QcJc on 2s5dJd two-tone). BB OOP at compressed SPR ~1.25 with 3-way action where opener/cold-caller both have wide ranges. Per the v2.3 calibration anchor in v3.4 Calibration Notes, d8886 is the donk-lead-or-mixed pattern: solver mixes BET/CHECK ~50/50. Betting 25% extracts thin value from Jx weaker kickers and pocket pairs, denies equity from overcards and backdoor flush hands. CHECK is fully defensible (pot control with TPGK OOP), making this difficulty 3.

Medium-made bucket (TPTK JcKs on Jd9d3h+6d turn 3-flush diamonds, hero has no diamond). Hero is PFA, flop checked through (villains showed weakness), turn brings third diamond. Per v2.3 calibration anchor in v3.4 Calibration Notes, d2410 is BET — top pair top kicker when checked to at compressed SPR with passive villains, even with the flush-completing turn. 75% sizing charges any single-diamond holding and extracts from worse Jx; checking risks giving free river cards on a flush-possible board.

Medium-made bucket (overpair JJ under K on Ks4h9c3h two-tone hearts). Hero is PFA OOP, flop checked, turn 3h adds 2-flush. Per v2.3 calibration anchor in v3.4 Calibration Notes, d8963 is solver 50/50 mixed BET; 33% small protective bet extracts from weaker pairs and denies overcard equity given villain_top_pair_plus_pct is lower than betting threshold (capped BTN range, no Kx 3-bets). CHECK considered — DO NOT Rule 11 paired-or-2-tone OOP carve-out leans CHECK with medium-made — making this difficulty 3 (both BET and CHECK explicitly evaluated).

Strong-made bucket (overpair AA on JhQcJcKs5h paired-board river). Both villains checked back turn (villain_checked_back action history). Per d3178 calibration anchor in v3.4 Calibration Notes, the river-checked-to override fires: AA on this runout BETs for value despite the paired board because villains have demonstrated weakness across two streets. 75% sizing extracts from Qx, Kx, JJ-trips slowplays (rare), and any Jx bluff-catcher; checking would burn the value of a clear overpair on a runout where villains' continuing-but-passive ranges are exploitable.
